cues.en: This is Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates. Two gentlemen fighting back and forth for the title of world's richest man. As of early twenty twenty, after a slump in Amazon stock price and a recent divorce, Bill Gates seems to be out ahead.
cues.zh: 这是Jeff Bezos和Bill Gates。两位绅士为了世界首富的头衔来回较量。到2020年初，在亚马逊股价下挫和近期离婚之后，Bill Gates似乎略占上风。

cues.en: But the recent price spike in Amazon stock means that Jeff Bezos could hold the title. I mean, it really is too hard to tell at this point.
cues.zh: 但亚马逊股价近期的飙升意味着Jeff Bezos可能保住这个头衔。我是说，眼下真的很难判断。

cues.en: These two individuals seem very, very similar on paper. For starters, of course, they are both billionaires,
cues.zh: 这两个人在纸面上看起来非常非常相似。首先，他们当然都是亿万富翁，

cues.en: an elite worldwide cub with around two and a half thousand members.
cues.zh: 属于全球约两千五百人的精英俱乐部。

cues.en: And more specifically,
cues.zh: 更具体地说，

cues.en: they are both white male tech entrepreneurs from The United States, and even more specifically than that, they're both from Seattle.
cues.zh: 他们都是来自美国的白人男性科技创业者，再更具体一点，他们俩都来自西雅图。

cues.en: And even more specifically, their primary residence is in Medina,
cues.zh: 再更具体一点，他们的主要住所都在Medina，

cues.en: a small town just outside of Seattle. So it looks like these two are extremely similar, but in reality, their fortunes couldn't be more different.
cues.zh: 那是西雅图郊外的一个小镇。所以看起来这两人极其相似，但实际上，他们的财富状况再不同不过了。

cues.en: A basic litmus test for this is to think about how they are accumulating money. At the moment, Gates' primary occupation is working as the chairman of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation,
cues.zh: 一个基本的试金石是想想他们如何积累财富。目前，Gates的主要职业是担任Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation的主席，

cues.en: which is a charitable foundation that more or less thinks up new and creative ways to give away money to worthy causes, and it does great work.
cues.zh: 这是一个慈善基金会，或多或少在想出新颖有创意的方式，把钱捐给有价值的事业，而且它做得非常出色。

cues.en: Jeff Bezos on the other hand is a little bit more tight fisted when it comes to things like charity.
cues.zh: 另一方面，Jeff Bezos在慈善这类事情上则有点抠门。

cues.en: Of course, this is not to say that Jeff Bezos has not given to charities. He has contributed a significant amount of money to some extremely worthwhile causes,
cues.zh: 当然，这并不是说杰夫·贝佐斯没有捐过慈善。他已经向一些极有价值的事业捐了一大笔钱，

cues.en: but it is nothing on the level of Gates, who has to date donated over 40,000,000,000
cues.zh: 但这和盖茨根本不是一个量级，盖茨迄今已向慈善机构捐赠超过400亿

cues.en: US dollars to charity.
cues.zh: 美元。

cues.en: Now this is not to say that Jeff Bezos is some Scrooge McDuck character.
cues.zh: 这也不是说杰夫·贝佐斯是某个史高治·麦克老鸭式的角色。

cues.en: It is just that Jeff Bezos
cues.zh: 只是杰夫·贝佐斯

cues.en: can't donate as much money as Gates simply
cues.zh: 没法像盖茨捐那么多钱，纯粹

cues.en: because he is a lower class of billionaire.
cues.zh: 因为他是更低一档的亿万富翁。

cues.en: And now hold up, I know what you might be thinking, but yes, there are very distinct classes of billionaires around the world.
cues.zh: 等等，我知道你可能在想什么，但没错，世界上的亿万富翁确实有非常分明的阶层。

cues.en: You are probably familiar with the colloquial
cues.zh: 你可能熟悉那种通俗的

cues.en: lower, middle, and upper class labels slapped onto people, mostly in developed countries, which are already upper class on a global standing, but it gets so much more granular than that.
cues.zh: 下层、中层、上层标签，主要被贴在发达国家的人身上，而这些人在全球范围内本就已属上层，但实际情况比这细致得多。

cues.en: And this isn't some weird conspiracy theory either.
cues.zh: 这也不是什么奇怪的阴谋论。

cues.en: Rankings amongst billionaires are not based on something as juvenile as net worth, but a range of factors that determine where they truly sit in the 0.0001%
cues.zh: 亿万富翁之间的排名不是基于净资产这种幼稚的东西，而是一系列决定他们真正处于0.0001%中什么位置的因素

cues.en: hierarchy.
cues.zh: 层级。

cues.en: What I want to do today is look at a select group of this select group and give you mere mortals watching an idea of how this is broken up and what truly classifies
cues.zh: 我今天想做的是看看这个精选群体中的一小部分人，让屏幕前身为凡人的你们大致了解这如何划分，以及真正决定

cues.en: a top billionaire.
cues.zh: 顶级亿万富翁的标准是什么。

cues.en: These are net worth, of course, it's still important, liquidity,
cues.zh: 这些标准是净资产，当然，这仍然重要，还有流动性、

cues.en: political power, and wealth security.
cues.zh: 政治权力和财富安全性。

cues.en: Which brings us on to our entry level billionaire.
cues.zh: 这就引出了我们的“入门级亿万富翁”。

cues.en: I wanna tell you a cool little trick that could legitimately give you a net worth of over $1,000,000,000
cues.zh: 我想教大家一个很酷的小把戏，能让你合法坐拥超过 10 亿美元的净资产，

cues.en: as the head of your own company.
cues.zh: 成为一家公司的掌门人。

cues.en: Go down to your local solicitors' offers, set up a limited liability shelf company, and make them create 10 shares in your company.
cues.zh: 去找你当地的律所，买一家有限责任空壳公司，让他们给公司发行 10 股股票。

cues.en: You keep nine shares yourself and place the tenth for sale for $100,000,000.
cues.zh: 你自己留 9 股，然后把第 10 股标价 1 亿美元出售。

cues.en: Congratulations.
cues.zh: 恭喜你。

cues.en: You now have a paper net worth of $1,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 你现在的账面身家已经达到 10 亿美元了。

cues.en: Now of course nobody would ever buy your worthless company share for $100,000,000,
cues.zh: 当然，根本不会有人花 1 亿美元买你这文不名值的股票，

cues.en: meaning your current equity position is really not worth $1,000,000,000
cues.zh: 这意味着你手里的股权实际上根本不值 10 亿美元，

cues.en: and you're not really a billionaire,
cues.zh: 你也算不上真正的亿万富翁，

cues.en: but this isn't actually too far from the reality for a lot of billionaires around the world.
cues.zh: 但对全球很多亿万富翁来说，现实其实也相差无几。

cues.en: Private companies are the primary vehicle that generate the wealth of most global billionaires.
cues.zh: 非上市公司正是全球大多数亿万富翁积累财富的主要载体。

cues.en: A private company is a limited liability company, the same as say Apple or Microsoft or Walmart,
cues.zh: 非上市公司同样是有限责任公司，就像 Apple、Microsoft 或 Walmart 一样，

cues.en: but they are not listed on public securities exchanges like the New York Stock Exchange, the NASDAQ, or any of the hundreds of other global stock exchanges.
cues.zh: 但它们并没有在纽约证券交易所、NASDAQ 或全球其他数百家证券交易所公开上市。

cues.en: This is not to say that these companies aren't big.
cues.zh: 这并不是说这些公司规模不大。

cues.en: Some of these private companies are every bit as large as all but the largest public companies,
cues.zh: 其中一些非上市公司的规模，完全不逊色于除极少数巨头之外的大多数上市公司，

cues.en: but it does limit things like influence,
cues.zh: 但这确实限制了它的影响力、

cues.en: wealth stability,
cues.zh: 财富稳定性，

cues.en: and above all, liquidity.
cues.zh: 以及最重要的——流动性。

cues.en: The Trump organisation is a fantastic
cues.zh: 特朗普集团就是一个绝佳的

cues.en: example of a privately owned company.
cues.zh: 私人控股公司的例子。

cues.en: Currently Donald Trump is the sole owner of all the shares in this company, which is in turn a conglomerate that owns over 500 other companies. Now while this business may be worth a lot, it is limited in terms of liquidity.
cues.zh: 目前，唐纳德·特朗普是该集团所有股份的唯一持有者，而该集团本身又是一个拥有500多家其他公司的大型企业集团。虽然这项业务可能价值不菲，但在流动性方面却相当有限。

cues.en: If Donald Trump wanted to go out and raise a billion dollars in cash tomorrow,
cues.zh: 如果唐纳德·特朗普想明天就筹集十亿美元现金，

cues.en: it would be very very difficult for him to do so. Being a sitting US president aside,
cues.zh: 那对他来说将非常非常困难。撇开他是现任美国总统这一点不谈，

cues.en: his company is not listed on any stock exchanges, meaning that he would have to create a market and court private investors to sell shares in the Trump organization too.
cues.zh: 他的公司没有在任何证券交易所上市，这意味着他必须自己创造一个市场，并争取私人投资者来购买特朗普集团的股份。

cues.en: What this means is that even though the Trump organization might be worth one or two or ten billion dollars on paper, it is very very difficult to turn that valuation
cues.zh: 这意味着，尽管特朗普集团在账面上可能价值十亿、二十亿甚至一百亿美元，但要想把这种估值

cues.en: into actual cash.
cues.zh: 变成实实在在的现金，是非常非常困难的。

cues.en: On top of this, a lot of the value of the Trump organization comes from Trump's name and the branding arrangement it can make with the figureheads of the business. Meaning that even if the company could be sold off, it may actually lose a significant amount of its value in doing so.
cues.zh: 除此之外，特朗普集团的很多价值来自特朗普这个名字，以及它可以与业务掌门人达成的品牌授权安排。这意味着，即使公司能够被出售，在出售过程中它实际上可能会损失相当大一部分价值。

cues.en: This is the predicament that a lot of private company billionaires find themselves in.
cues.zh: 这就是许多私营企业亿万富翁所处的困境。

cues.en: Great paper fortunes without being able to recognise any of this wealth or turn it into cash to buy mansions or jets or super yachts. You know, it's a hard not life indeed.
cues.zh: 账面上有巨额财富，却无法兑现其中任何一部分，也无法将其转化为现金去购买豪宅、私人飞机或超级游艇。你知道，这日子可真不好过啊。

cues.en: Don't feel too bad for these guys though. Often times their companies run great profits that mean that they are still bringing in a lot of cash every year, but some actually don't.
cues.zh: 不过，也不用太为这些家伙感到难过。通常情况下，他们的公司利润丰厚，这意味着他们每年依然能赚到大把的现金，但实际上有些公司却并非如此。

cues.en: A lot of tech startups in particular
cues.zh: 尤其是很多科技初创公司

cues.en: tend to run at a loss for the first few years of their operations.
cues.zh: 在运营的头几年往往会亏损。

cues.en: Think of companies like snapchat,
cues.zh: 想想Snapchat这样的公司，

cues.en: instagram or linkedin. The founders of these companies often take a $1 a year salary and their companies are running at a loss. So while they are billionaires on paper,
cues.zh: Instagram或LinkedIn。这些公司的创始人往往只拿1美元年薪，公司还在亏损运营。所以尽管他们纸面上是亿万富翁，

cues.en: they take home less money than the janitor.
cues.zh: 他们带回家的钱比看门人还要少。

cues.en: It's not all bad though. Some benefits of running a private company is that you are not at liberty to make financial statements publicly available,
cues.zh: 不过也不全是坏事。经营私有公司的一些好处是，你不必公开财务报表，

cues.en: which offers a level of anonymity that a lot of these individuals prefer over public companies that have every balance sheet, every income statement analysed by the public.
cues.zh: 这就提供了一定程度的匿名性，相比每一张资产负债表和利润表都要被公众审视的上市公司，很多人更青睐这一点。

cues.en: And again,
cues.zh: 再说一次，

cues.en: try not to feel too bad for these guys otherwise.
cues.zh: 不过也别太替这些人难过。

cues.en: There is actually an entire private banking industry designed around accommodating
cues.zh: 实际上，存在一个完整的私人银行业，专门为了迎合

cues.en: for these individuals.
cues.zh: 对这些人来说。

cues.en: Say the founder of super cool growth at all cost tech star up incorporated wants to buy a new private jet. Well, he doesn't have any money because his entire net worth is tied up in a company that is not publicly tradable
cues.zh: 假设这家追求极致增长、不惜一切代价的科技明星初创公司的创始人想买一架新的私人飞机。可他没钱，因为他的全部身家都绑在一家未公开交易的公司里。

cues.en: and is running at a loss. They also don't receive a salary,
cues.zh: 而且处于亏损状态。他们也没有薪水，

cues.en: so what they do instead is this,
cues.zh: 所以他们转而这样做，

cues.en: call up their private banker and say hey, I need a line of credit for $60,000,000.
cues.zh: 打电话给他们的私人银行家说，嘿，我需要一笔六千万美元的信贷额度。

cues.en: Okay, you know, to buy a jet. And the banker would ask, okay, do you have a down payment? Any income verification or a strong credit file? To which mister tech entrepreneur would say, I have no down payment. I earn $1 a year and I don't have a credit file.
cues.zh: 你看，买喷气机。银行家会问，好吧，你有首付吗？有收入证明或良好的信用记录吗？这位科技企业家会说，我没有首付。我一年只赚1美元，也没有信用记录。

cues.en: Now if this were a mere mortal like you or I applying for a car loan, we would get laughed out of the dealership.
cues.zh: 如果换成像你我这样的普通人去申请车贷，我们会当场被经销商嘲笑出门。

cues.en: But it turns out that banks are a little bit more accommodating of rich people. They basically offer a line of credit to these individuals under the impression that one day they will sell their company and be able to pay it all back.
cues.zh: 但事实证明，银行对有钱人更通融一些。他们基本上会给这些人提供信用额度，觉得他们总有一天会卖掉公司，把欠款全部还清。

cues.en: This is basically a loan that you don't have to pay back for a very very long time. Sure, it accumulates interest, but you don't even have to pay that back until you are ready to. This allows paper billionaires to live lavish before they really made any money at all.
cues.zh: 这基本上是一笔很长时间都不用还的贷款。当然，它会累积利息，但你甚至都不用还利息，直到你准备好为止。这让纸面上的亿万富翁在真正赚到钱之前就能过上奢华生活。

cues.en: Remember this man, Jeff Bezos? Well, he actually epitomizes
cues.zh: 还记得这个人吗，Jeff Bezos？他其实就是一个典型

cues.en: a middle class billionaire.
cues.zh: 中产阶级亿万富翁。

cues.en: And I know, on paper, he may be one of, if not the richest man in the world, but he also has almost his entire fortune
cues.zh: 我知道，从账面上看，他可能是世界上最富有的人之一，甚至就是最富的，但他几乎全部财富

cues.en: wrapped up in a single company.
cues.zh: 都集中在一家公司里。

cues.en: Now it is a very, very big company granted,
cues.zh: 当然，这是一家非常非常大的公司，

cues.en: but it is still a single company.
cues.zh: 但它仍然只是一家公司。

cues.en: Middle class billionaires tend to be large stakeholders in post IPO
cues.zh: 中产阶级亿万富翁往往是IPO后公司的

cues.en: companies.
cues.zh: 大股东。

cues.en: Things like Facebook's Mark Zuckerberg or Amazon's Jeff Bezos.
cues.zh: 比如Facebook的Mark Zuckerberg，或者Amazon的Jeff Bezos。

cues.en: They still attribute a majority of their wealth to a single company,
cues.zh: 他们仍将大部分财富归功于一家公司，

cues.en: but it is a public company.
cues.zh: 但这是一家上市公司。

cues.en: What that means is that it allows these individuals to actually get cash for themselves by selling off portions of their company ownership onto public stock exchanges.
cues.zh: 这意味着，这些人可以通过将公司所有权的一部分出售到公开股票交易所，从而真正为自己获取现金。

cues.en: For example Jeff Bezos cashes out about $2,000,000,000
cues.zh: 例如，杰夫·贝索斯每年套现约20亿美元的亚马逊股票，

cues.en: worth of Amazon stock every year to pay for everyday billionaire stuff, as well as to contribute towards other projects like his space project Blue Origin.
cues.zh: 用于支付日常的亿万富翁开销，以及资助其他项目，比如他的太空项目蓝色起源。

cues.en: There are still limitations on this class of billionaire though. They are still at the mercy of a single company. If Amazon filed for bankruptcy tomorrow, Jeff Bezos would lose a vast majority of his fortune, meaning that their wealth is a little bit more unstable.
cues.zh: 不过，这一类亿万富翁仍有局限。他们仍然受制于一家公司。如果亚马逊明天申请破产，杰夫·贝索斯将失去绝大部分财富，这意味着他们的财富稍微更不稳定。

cues.en: Overall though, middle class billionaires that own public companies tend to have a higher net worth than those who own private companies. They have more liquidity because they can sell their shares onto the public market. They have more political influence because they are powerful figures in institutions that can impact a whole economy.
cues.zh: 但总体而言，拥有上市公司的中产阶级亿万富翁，其净资产往往高于拥有私营公司的亿万富翁。他们流动性更强，因为可以把股票卖到公开市场。他们的政治影响力更大，因为他们是能够影响整个经济的机构中的强势人物。

cues.en: Jeff Bezos, for example, had cities fighting over him and his company when a decision was being made about where Amazon's second global headquarters should be located.
cues.zh: 例如，在决定亚马逊第二全球总部选址时，杰夫·贝索斯曾让多个城市争相争取他和他的公司。

cues.en: But all of this aside,
cues.zh: 但抛开这一切不谈，

cues.en: they are still
cues.zh: 他们仍然

cues.en: less liquid and less secure than the next level of billionaires.
cues.zh: 比下一层级的亿万富翁流动性更差、安全性更低。

cues.en: Microsoft
cues.zh: Microsoft

cues.en: has more than tripled in value in the last five years, which would go a long way to explaining why mister Bill Gates' wealth has grown so much in recent years despite his best attempts to give it all away.
cues.zh: 过去五年市值增长了两倍多，这很大程度上解释了为什么比尔·盖茨先生的财富近年来增长如此之多，尽管他竭尽全力想要全部捐出去。

cues.en: And it would go a long way to explaining it if it weren't completely untrue.
cues.zh: 这本来能很好地解释这一点——如果不是完全不对的话。

cues.en: You see, Bill Gates is an upper middle class billionaire.
cues.zh: 你看，比尔·盖茨其实是个中上阶层的亿万富翁。

cues.en: His wealth is actually almost completely divested from Microsoft shares. It doesn't even make up a quarter of his portfolio anymore.
cues.zh: 他的财富实际上几乎已经完全从微软股票中剥离出来。微软股票甚至占不到他投资组合的四分之一。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: he is almost like his own hedge fund.
cues.zh: 他几乎就像自己的对冲基金。

cues.en: The Gates family office is a company that operates exclusively
cues.zh: 盖茨家族办公室是一家专门运营的公司，

cues.en: to invest the wealth of Bill and Melinda Gates, and his company has invested into a wide array of companies that provides the Gate family with strong income returns as well as offering diversity
cues.zh: 负责投资比尔和梅琳达·盖茨的财富，这家公司投资了众多企业，为盖茨家族带来强劲的收益回报，同时提供多元化

cues.en: and stability in a portfolio.
cues.zh: 和稳定的投资组合。

cues.en: This means that Gates can easily raise a lot of cash very quickly by selling off stocks in many companies without crashing their individual markets,
cues.zh: 这意味着盖茨可以通过抛售多家公司的股票迅速筹集大量现金，而不会导致这些公司的市场崩盘，

cues.en: and also has a wider spread of influence over a diverse range of companies in different areas.
cues.zh: 同时还能在不同领域的众多公司中拥有更广泛的影响力。

cues.en: This is the logical end goal of most western billionaires.
cues.zh: 这是大多数西方亿万富翁的合理终极目标。

cues.en: Start a really really successful company,
cues.zh: 创办一家非常非常成功的公司，

cues.en: slowly sell it off, and turn that paper wealth into tangible wealth with a well diversified
cues.zh: 慢慢把它卖掉，把那些纸面财富转化为有形财富，配上多元化良好

cues.en: and stable portfolio of investments.
cues.zh: 且稳定的投资组合。

cues.en: The billionaires that achieve this level tend to be further on in their careers.
cues.zh: 达到这一层次的亿万富翁，往往处于职业生涯的更后期阶段。

cues.en: Think Sergey Brin of Google, Larry Ellison of Oracle, Bill Gates of Microsoft, Warren Buffett of Berkshire Hathaway and, yeah, even people like, say, Jay Z and Beyonce.
cues.zh: 想想Google的Sergey Brin、Oracle的Larry Ellison、Microsoft的Bill Gates、Berkshire Hathaway的Warren Buffett，甚至还有像Jay Z和Beyonce这样的人。

cues.en: And you might think, at this point, it can't get much better. These billionaires have almost unlimited access to cash. Their asset position is very secure, they can have huge political influence if they choose to exercise this power, and they have net worth that seems to accumulate
cues.zh: 到这一步你可能觉得，已经不能再好了。这些亿万富翁几乎有取之不尽的现金。他们的资产地位非常稳固，只要愿意，就能拥有巨大的政治影响力，而且他们的净资产似乎还在不断累积，

cues.en: regardless of how hard they try to give their money away.
cues.zh: 不管他们多想把钱送出去都挡不住。

cues.en: But there is still a level of billionaires even above these guys.
cues.zh: 但在这群人之上，还有更高一层的亿万富翁。

cues.en: Welcome to the true old money elite.
cues.zh: 欢迎来到真正的老钱精英阶层。

cues.en: This is a class of individual that have been wealthy for generations.
cues.zh: 这个阶层的人已经富了好几代。

cues.en: They are royals or nobility or from a lineage of wealth that extends back to recorded history. They don't own companies, they own countries.
cues.zh: 他们是皇室或贵族，或者出身于可追溯到有记载历史的财富世系。他们不拥有公司，他们拥有国家。

cues.en: They are Saudi royals or Russian oligarchs, European nobility, or American old money. A lot of these individuals don't show up on things like Forbes lists for a few reasons.
cues.zh: 他们是沙特皇室或俄罗斯寡头、欧洲贵族或美国老钱。这些人中有很多不会出现在福布斯榜单之类的地方，原因有几个。

cues.en: Firstly, their wealth is a lot harder to quantify. To work out Jeff Bezos' wealth, for example, it's very very easy.
cues.zh: 首先，他们的财富要量化起来难得多。比如要算出Jeff Bezos的财富，非常简单。

cues.en: The market capitalization of Amazon times 16 for his ownership stake, plus maybe some incidental billions as a margin of error, and tada,
cues.zh: Amazon的市值乘以16就是他的持股，再加上也许几十亿的偶然误差，然后——

cues.en: there is his net worth. Slap it on the Forbes list.
cues.zh: 他的净资产就出来了。往福布斯榜单上一放就行。

cues.en: Upper class billionaires
cues.zh: 上层亿万富翁

cues.en: don't really hold wealth like this though. They will be one and the same thing with national treasuries,
cues.zh: 可不是这么持有财富的。他们往往和国家金库融为一体，

cues.en: they will directly own state enterprises that aren't open to the general public to buy, and they do their darndest to fly under the radar.
cues.zh: 他们直接拥有普通公众买不到的国家企业，而且他们竭尽全力保持低调。

cues.en: Oftentimes,
cues.zh: 通常，

cues.en: these individuals lord over countries that are quite poor.
cues.zh: 这些人统治着非常贫穷的国家。

cues.en: It is a bit of a bad look for a multi multi billionaire to be flexing in western media if your constituents are struggling to feed themselves,
cues.zh: 如果你的选民还在为温饱苦苦挣扎，一个身家数百亿的超级富豪却在西方媒体上炫富，这未免有些不太好看，

cues.en: but it does show in a few places.
cues.zh: 但这在某些地方确实屡见不鲜。

cues.en: You ever wonder who these people are buying
cues.zh: 你有没有想过，都是什么人在买

cues.en: billion dollar super yachts or $500,000,000
cues.zh: 价值十亿美元的超级游艇，或是五亿美元的

cues.en: paintings?
cues.zh: 画作？

cues.en: Well, they are the people from the upper class of billionaires.
cues.zh: 嗯，他们正是亿万富豪中的上层阶级。

cues.en: Need liquidity?
cues.zh: 需要流动资金？

cues.en: It's not a matter of doing anything as common as selling your shares in an open market. You just ring up the treasury department of your own nation.
cues.zh: 这根本不需要去公开市场卖股票这么俗气。你只需给本国的财政部打个电话就行。

cues.en: Wealth stability is crazy high as well. Normally these individuals are so well diversified and their money is so entrenched into national industries
cues.zh: 财富稳定性也高得离谱。通常这些人资产配置极其多元，他们的资金与国家产业深度绑定，

cues.en: that the only way they are going broke is taking an entire nation down with them. As for political influence,
cues.zh: 以至于他们破产的唯一方式，就是拉着整个国家一起陪葬。至于政治影响力，

cues.en: well, I mean, they are either oligarchs pulling the strings of government or they are direct heads of state. So it doesn't get much better than that.
cues.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，他们要么是操控政府的寡头，要么就是国家元首。所以权势再大也就不过如此了。

cues.en: Now the net worth of these individuals may on paper be lower, either through creative hiding of it off their books to avoid scrutiny or because it has just been diluted amongst hundreds of family members that share the lineage of the wealth. They actually kind of have the opposite problem of lower class billionaires.
cues.zh: 现在，这些人的净资产在纸面上可能会低一些，这可能是通过在账外巧妙隐藏以躲避审查，或者是由于财富在数百名同宗的家族成员中被稀释了。他们的处境其实有点像底层亿万富豪的反面。

cues.en: No paper wealth at all, but almost unlimited
cues.zh: 纸面财富全无，

cues.en: money and power at their disposal.
cues.zh: 但却能调动几乎无限的资金和权力。

cues.en: Now this of course all sounds a bit tinfoil hatty, like I am one step away from talking about the lizard people that secretly rule the world. But oddly enough though, these classes of billionaires are very very widely recognised amongst groups in high financing circles.
cues.zh: 当然，这听起来有点像是阴谋论，感觉我离谈论统治世界的蜥蜴人只有一步之遥。但奇怪的是，在高端金融圈子里，这类亿万富翁群体其实得到了非常广泛的认可。

cues.en: Wealth inequality is a hotly debated issue worldwide
cues.zh: 财富不平等是全球热议的话题

cues.en: and it is of course no excuse at all to say that any of these individuals are hard done by monetarily.
cues.zh: 当然，这绝不能成为替这些人在金钱上过得艰难而开脱的借口。

cues.en: But it is still very very interesting to understand the dynamic of how this very foreign world works.
cues.zh: 不过，去理解这个极其陌生的世界是如何运作的，依然是一件非常非常有趣的事。

cues.en: So before you feel like complaining about your minimum wage job not covering your crippling repayments on your student loan debt, spare a thought for the tech billionaire that can't even afford to feed himself or fuel his jet without taking out a personal loan.
cues.zh: 所以，在你抱怨自己拿最低工资的工作还不起沉重的学生贷款之前，不妨体谅一下那位科技亿万富翁——他如果不申请个人贷款，甚至都吃不起饭，或者给自己的私人飞机加不起油。
